driver-layers.title: Three layers, one of them yours
driver-layers.alt: Layer diagram: the application calls the hardware-agnostic MCP9700 driver, which relies on the ADC adapter contract, which the platform adapter you write fulfils, which reads the MCU's ADC connected to the MCP9700's analog output.
driver-layers.description: From top to bottom. Your application talks to one Mcp9700Thermistor<AdcType> object per sensor, whose public calls (listed from inc/mcp9700_thermistor.hpp) initialise the ADC and return degrees Celsius. The core turns one ADC voltage into a temperature with (V - v_zero_c) / v_per_c. The ADC adapter contract is the template parameter: any class with the two methods named in the header's documentation, checked at compile time. The platform port is the only code you write: that class, which brings your ADC up and returns the voltage at the sensor's VOUT pin. Below it is the hardware.
